items.title: Jackie Cain and Roy Kral interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, March 22, 1998
items.q: we made that album “Time and Love,” which is the album we did for Creed Taylor, and that was such a wonderful time.

ctx.x: — that it was just uplifting. This wonderful music we were making together. So all of a sudden the joy of making music, making good music with a group is a great experience.

It saved our lives, you know, it saved us. But you know one thing we did leave out, I just remembered that the year before this all happened in 1972 is when we made that album “Time and Love,” which is the album we did for Creed Taylor, and that was such a wonderful time. We were going out to Fire Island in the summer. We were renting a house with our friend Bradley Cunningham, and we’d spent three months out there. And we hadn’t been doing anything because we were doing the commercials. So at one point we said…

We’d done maybe four albums for him on Verve and so forth, and we were going to go into the city and just like talk it up — Creed we want to do another album, and like let’s see what we can do, and so we walked in and we started talking, talking, talking, and he says, “that sounds like a good idea, let’s do it.”
